# 01 — What you want

The top row of every power map. Fill this in once, edit it when it changes.

The skill reads this before it reads the thread, so it knows what a good outcome looks like
before it starts optimising for one. Left blank, it will optimise for the outcome the
counterparty wants, because theirs is the only one written down anywhere.

---

## What you are actually holding

Anything a counterparty cannot easily get elsewhere. Be specific and use real numbers.

| Asset | Figure | Why it is leverage |
|---|---|---|
| [Audience / list / channel] | [number] | [why they cannot easily replace it] |
| [Second channel] | [number] | [what makes it distinct — a demographic, an engagement rate] |
| [Owned list — email, newsletter] | [number] | Owned. Nobody can throttle it |
| [Third-party proof — press, awards, logos] | [names] | Removes "who are you" before the conversation starts |
| [Your company / legal entity] | [structure] | You contract as a business, not an individual |
| [Delivery capacity — team, contractors] | [number] | Whether you are the bottleneck |
| [Track record — streak, years, volume] | [figure] | Nobody negotiating with you can wait you out |

## What you charge

[List them flatly. Rate per deliverable, minimums, what you will not do at any price.]

**Also list what sits BELOW your headline rate.** This is the row people leave empty and it is
the one that saves deals: when someone names a number under your rate, you need one line you can
put beside your rate that they can actually buy. Without it, every counter reads as a decline.

| Deliverable | Price |
|---|---|
| [Headline offer] | [rate] |
| [The step down] | [rate] |
| [The small one] | [rate] |

## What you actually want from a deal like this

Not just money. Rank them, because a play trades one for another:

1. [e.g. money]
2. [e.g. the relationship, because they introduce you to others]
3. [e.g. the logo, because it removes "who are you" from the next five conversations]
4. [e.g. speed — done and off your desk]

**If you do not rank these, every play optimises for money by default,** and that is wrong often
enough to matter.
